content:
I haven't created placeholder discussions for these yet, but I think these are all things that need discussing soon! If something on this list interests you, please create a new topic for it and take the lead.

  • Scaling review: how many review agents are needed to keep up with contributions? We need people to run these review agents, and possibly to provide the resources (inference and CI compute) to run them at scale.
  • Tracking progress on roadmaps: how do we tell where through a roadmap we are, without reading all the code? We need some metadata, but it needs to be lightweight and flexible, and compatible with humans writing roadmaps as unannotated markdown.
  • Maintenance: I've already done a few Mathlib bumps via agents. This is definitely viable, but needs good automation. What other maintenance tasks do we want to tackle?
  • Refactoring: we're going to find problems (horrible, nauseating problems!) in the library as it grows. How are we going to address these? Issues to fix things, updates to review rubrics, subject-area prompting, etc, etc?
  • Summarisation/documentation/findability: Should we write AI overviews of material? Reference manuals? Searchable indexes? Can we get Tau Ceti into the various semantic search tools? Run a loogle instance?
  • Auditing of definitions: can we prepare some sort of overlay system for human auditing of chains of definitions. @Rémy Degenne has ideas in this direction. Hopefully this could be a project-agnostic system that Tau Ceti participates in, rather than tied to Tau Ceti. (See discussion continuing at #Tau Ceti > Auditing definitions.)
  • Evaluation of review: it would be great to be able to evaluate the performance of different models as review agents, and to be able to quantitatively measure the how effective the review rubrics are. The TauCetiData repository contains all the reviews in machine readable form, with all their metadata. I've started some experiments doing A/B testing of reviews, with AI judges + human labelling, but I need people to run with this if it's going to be useful.
